claims.harm: Header drags addrman, key_io, and protocol into tests that do not need them, increasing preprocessed lines and causing unnecessary recompilations
claims.quote: feefrac_tests and txgraph_tests only need the FeeFrac printers, but this block drags addrman, key_io and protocol in with it. Touching addrman now rebuilds both, and it's about 12k extra preprocessed lines in the first one. Would it be worth splitting this by area?
claims.settled_by_quote: Added common.cpp with the implementations and all forward delc to common.h in latest push

claims.harm: Printers omit fields compared by operator==, causing failed checks to display identical values or generic types without diagnostic detail
claims.quote: This one leaves out nTime and nServices, which operator== does compare, so in the two addrv1/addrv2 unserialize checks a regression in time or in flags comes out as [::1]:0 != [::1]:0. The CTxDestination one prints CTxDestination() for CNoDestination and PubKeyDestination.
claims.settled_by_quote: Added additional info for CAddress and took a glance through the rest of the ==, I think all fields should be covered. As far as CTxDestination, I added specific displays for each variant and the CTxDestination printer now just passes through to those.

claims.harm: Encode asserts on an empty key, causing bip32_tests to abort with SIGABRT instead of reporting failure and continuing the suite
claims.quote: Encode() asserts on an empty key, which is what DecodeExtKey leaves you with when it fails, and that's the value bip32_tests compares. I broke the decode to see. The case dies on SIGABRT and takes the following ones with it.
claims.settled_by_quote: Yes, that's what I meant. I broke the decode again and now it prints CExtKey(<invalid>) and the suite finishes, no SIGABRT.

claims.harm: ScriptToAsmStr decodes small pushes as numbers, allowing scripts that differ in bytes to display identical string representations on failure
claims.quote: ScriptToAsmStr decodes any push of up to four bytes as a number, so scripts that differ in bytes can come out as the same string... Would it be worth adding hex=%s alongside?
claims.settled_by_quote: added the hex string alongside the ASM in the latest push
